newsitem.title: UK: UK FOA says master netting accord almost ready.
newsitem.headline: UK FOA says master netting accord almost ready.

text.p: The UK Futures and Options Association (FOA) says it has almost completed a master netting accord to permit firms dealing in exchange-traded derivatives to meet new UK rules without having to hold much greater capital.

A tough new capital adequacy regime involving commodity and futures firms with clients in countries that do not have legally binding netting agreements had been sought by the UK Securities and Futures Authority (SFA).
Earlier this year some firms calculated that the new SFA regime would require over 60 times the amount of capital now needed to conduct the same volume of business.

The FOA said in a statement on Thursday that it was now near completion of a project, begun with support from 60 firms, to develop its master agreement in response to the new SFA rules for firms netting risk in exchange-traded transactions.

The FOA said it believed the emerging accord, in 35 key jurisdictions around the globe where favourable legal opinion on its enforceability had been obtained, would enable firms to secure the benefit of lower capital adequacy based on their net -not gross- positions.
"Netting risk" is the risk that firms' netting arrangements with their customers would be susceptible to challenge by a liquidator in the event of a customer default.

Profitable transactions could be claimed by a liquidator of the customer for the benefit of its creditors. The firm could be left to claim for the gross amount of their unprofitable transactions in the liquidation.
The FOA is a trade association for firms and individuals who carry on business in futures, options or other derivatives. It has an international membership of some 200.
FOA chairman Sir Michael Jenkiuns said it was "a remarkable achievement" to have completed a major international project in just over 12 months.
